# ParseFailure

A parsing failure that can say where it happened.

```rux
pub interface ParseFailure {
    func Offset() -> uint;
}
```

Every domain owns its own parse error, because what went wrong in a UUID and what went wrong in a timestamp are
different questions with different answers, and flattening them into one type would lose the distinctions a
caller acts on. What they share is the position, and that is what this names.
The offset is a zero-based UTF-8 byte offset into the text that was handed to the parser. End of input is the
text's length, which is a position and not a failure to have one. A parser embedded in a larger grammar adds the
offset of the token it was given, so positions compose.

## Requirements

<h3 id="offset"><code>Offset</code></h3>

```rux
func Offset() -> uint
```

Where in the input the failure was found.

**Returns**: the zero-based UTF-8 byte offset, which is the text's length at end of input
